paper.title: Online Minimization of Polarization and Disagreement via Low-Rank Matrix Bandits

unmapped: Low-rank (rank-one, symmetric PSD Theta* = s s^T) matrix bandit: actions are |V|x|V| forest matrices (I+L)^{-1} of graph Laplacians, loss <Theta*, X> (trace inner product), loss minimization
Learner knows the RSC curvature kappa and the signal strength ||s||^2 (or a lower bound ell_s) to tune the exploration length T1
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal{L} = \{\mat{L}_1, \dots, \mat{L}_K\}$ be the intervention space... $f(\mat{X}) = \langle \mat{\Theta}^*, \mat{X}\rangle$... The learner observes bandit feedback in the form of a noisy loss signal: $Y_t = f(\mat{X}_t) + \eta_t$, where $\eta_t \sim N(0,\sigma^2)$... $R_T = \sum_{t=1}^T ( f(\mat{X}_t) - f(\mat{X}^*) )$.

symbols.kappa: RSC curvature constant (kappa_min of the arm set over the cone)

conditions: RSC condition (Assumption 2) holds with curvature kappa and 128 tau^2_{T1} <= kappa
Theta* = s s^T rank one, s in [-1,1]^|V| mean-centered
T sufficiently large: T >= T_0 ~ ||s||^4/kappa^2 log(2|V|/delta)
tuning: Stage-2 linear bandit subroutine with regret O~(k sqrt T), k = 2|V|-1 (e.g. OFUL)

source.label: thm:main regret
source.quote: Suppose the subspace linear bandit algorithm used in Stage~2 enjoys $R^{\mathrm{sub}}_T= \tilde{\mathcal{O}}(k \sqrt{T})$, where $ k = 2\dimension - 1 $. Under \Cref{assum: RSC}, for any failure probability $\delta \in (0, 1)$ and an optimally chosen number of exploration rounds $T_1 \asymp \frac{1}{\|\innateopinions\|^2 \kappa} \sqrt{T\log(2\dimension/\delta)})$, the total regret ... over sufficiently large $T \ge T_0 \asymp \frac{\|\innateopinions\|^4}{\kappa^2} \log(2\dimension/\delta)$ rounds satisfies, with probability at least $ 1 - \delta $, $R_T = \widetilde{\mathcal{O}} ( \max\{\frac{ 1}{\kappa}, \sqrt{ \dimension } \} \sqrt{ \dimension \cdot T})$

results.notes: Regret defined via expected losses f(X_t) (pseudo-regret type) but holds w.p. 1-delta. Mapped to linear_finite with low-rank parameter structure; ambient dimension is |V|^2.

conditions: same assumptions as Theorem 4.1 (RSC, rank-one Theta*, sigma = 1, T large enough)
||s||^2 >= ell_s with ell_s known; proof uses ell_s = Omega(|V|)
tuning: T1 ~ sqrt(T log(2|V|/delta)) / (ell_s kappa) (proof: 6/(ell_s kappa) sqrt(T log(2|V|/delta)))

source.label: cor:regret_with_lower_bound
source.quote: Under the same assumptions as \Cref{thm:main regret}, suppose that the true signal strength $\|\innateopinions\|^2$ is unknown, but a lower bound $\ell_s > 0$ is known, such that $\|\innateopinions\|^2 \ge \ell_s$. If we set the exploration phase length $T_1 \asymp \frac{1}{\ell_s\,\kappa}\,\sqrt{T\,\log\frac{2\dimension}{\delta}}$, then the total regret $R_T$ is bounded by: $R_T =\tilde{\mathcal{O}}( \frac{1}{\kappa } \sqrt{\dimension \cdot T})$.

results.notes: Recorded as stated. The proof's final line drops the c(k) sqrt(T) = O~(|V| sqrt T) in-subspace term, so the statement looks inconsistent with Theorem 4.1 unless 1/kappa >= sqrt(|V|). High probability inherited from Theorem 4.1.
